definitions.explanation: A casual first-person plural used mainly by younger speakers and by women, and widely in Kansai speech regardless of gender. It emphasizes the speaker's own circle as against other people.

examples.japanese: うちら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦クラス→クラス：01084_kurasu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Our class has a lot of boys.

examples.japanese: うちら⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ずっと→ずっと：00912_zutto⟧⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦{部活|ぶかつ}→部活：05377_bukatsu⟧だった⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{言|い}わなくて→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{気持|きも}ち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: We were in the same club the whole time, so we know how each other feels without saying it.

notes:
USAGE:
From うち (I, casual) plus the plural suffix 〜ら. Strictly informal: appropriate among friends and classmates, but out of place at work, in writing, or with anyone senior, where ⟦{私|わたし}たち→私たち：28351_watashitachi⟧ is required.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{私|わたし}たち→私たち：28351_watashitachi⟧: we — the neutral, all-purpose form
- ⟦{僕|ぼく}ら→僕ら：22784_bokura⟧: we — casual, male speakers
- ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧ら: we — rough and masculine
- うち: I — the singular this is built on, casual and common among girls and in Kansai
